sentences.text: For Appellants : Mr.D.Nitin  in both appeals  For Respondent : Mr. S. Sathia Seelan  in both appeals  COMMON JUDGMENT
Challenging the order passed by the Tribunal, the Transport Corporation preferred these appeals.

2.The learned counsel for the appellant/Transport Corporation submitted that the Tribunal failed to take into account the fact that the rider of the two wheeler possessed a valid driving license or not.

In fact, without license, the rider of the two wheeler drove the vehicle at the time accident and without verifying the genuineness of the Medical Bills, the Tribunal has taken into consideration the entire Medical Bills and also without any documentary proof, the Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads.
Hence, he prayed to set aside the findings of the Tribunal.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 08/07/2025 05:27:13 pm ) C.M.A.Nos.967 and 968 of 2023 3.The

learned counsel for the respondents submitted that before the Tribunal, the respondents have produced all the relevant materials and based on that only, the Tribunal has fixed the liability as well as awarded compensation which need no interference.
4.The main contentions raised on the side of the appellant is that at the time of accident, the rider of the two wheeler has not possessed a valid driving license.
Before the Tribunal, they have not raised such a defence.
On the other hand, they produced all the material documents.

5.In fact, the accident was taken place due to the negligent driving of the driver of the Bus and an FIR has been lodged against the driver of the Bus and to prove the manner of the accident,
appropriate evidence has been adduced.
Therefore, the negligence on the part of the driver of the Bus was proved.
Hence, the objections raised by the appellant, as such, is unsustainable.
6.Accordingly, both the Civil Miscellaneous Appeals are dismissed as no merits.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
